why: A player with no matching Hero to reveal gains one Wound to their discard pile — reveal-or-wound applies gainWound only when the hero-trait predicate is unmet (D-24281).
A player holding a matching X-Men Hero in hand reveals it for free and gains no Wound (D-24281).

The reveal predicate scans hand union in-play, not hand alone (the 2026-07-31 amendment): a matching Hero already played this turn sits in in-play and still spares the Wound. A hand-only regression would wrongly wound this player (D-24281).
Ymir's Fight KOs every Wound from the current player's hand and discard pile to the general KO pile — the two hand Wounds then the discard Wound all land in G.ko (D-24329).
The scan is hand + discard only, never in-play — a Wound in play is left untouched (Wounds are never played into in-play; D-24329 narrowing 2). The hand Wound is still KO'd, so the handler did run.

Melter's Fight is now an interactive per-card KO/keep choice (D-24413, superseding the D-24332 auto-resolve): revealing the deck tops KOs nothing at park time — the KO waits for the player's resolve. The old auto-resolve would have culled the revealed Wound immediately.
Melter's Fight parks exactly one PendingMelterKoChoice for the fighting player, carrying every revealed deck top (D-24413, active-player-scoped choice).
Resolving a Melter choice with keep=false KOs the chosen revealed card from its owner's deck top to the KO pile (D-24413).
Resolving a Melter choice with keep=true is a KO no-op — the card was never removed and stays face-up on top of its owner's deck (D-24413, the printed 'or put it back').

The optional-ko-reward KO source now includes in-play (hand union discard union in-play): a card played this turn can be KO'd for the reward — the classic deck-thinning play the printed hand-or-discard wording excluded (D-24442).
KO'ing an in-play card still dispatches the reward (here rescue, moving one Bystander to the Victory pile); the KO does not claw back the value the played card already produced (D-24442).
A dual-class card counts as its SECOND printed class: Ruby Summers 'Heir to Legends' (Strength + Ranged) satisfies a Ranged test (D-24523).
A dual-class card still counts as its FIRST printed class — the second class is additive, not a replacement (D-24523).
A dual-class card matches ONLY its two printed classes: a class it does not print (Tech) returns false, so the dual-class change grants no phantom membership (D-24523).
gain-wound with target 'each-other' wounds every player except the current one; the non-current player gains exactly one Wound to their discard, proving the effect fired (D-24295, the Lizard).

The current (fighting) player is excluded from an 'each-other' wound and gains nothing — the seat-exclusion a hand-rolled each-player loop gets wrong. Paired with gain-wound-each-other-wounds-other-player, which proves the handler ran (D-24295).

A zone-restricted each-player ko-hero (Juggernaut) KOs only from the named source zone (discard); with magnitude 2 but one Hero in discard it KOs that Hero and stops — it does NOT fall back to hand (D-24280).

The hand Hero is untouched by a discard-restricted KO even when the KO count exceeds the discard's Hero supply — the no-fallback source restriction (D-24280). Paired with the positive sibling that asserts the discard Hero was KO'd.
Viper's conditional each-player wound: a player with no other HYDRA Villain in their Victory pile gains one Wound to their discard (D-24299).

A player who already holds ANOTHER HYDRA Villain in their Victory pile is spared the Wound — the anchored group-prefix membership test excludes the just-fought Viper. Paired with the positive sibling that proves the handler wounds an unprotected player (D-24299).
The counted capture-bystander (Abomination, magnitude 3) rescues N Bystanders and, on Fight, awards them immediately to the defeating player's Victory pile (D-24295).
The counted rescue is bounded by the Bystander supply: with magnitude 3 but only two Bystanders available, exactly two are rescued and the loop stops (D-24295).
A location-gated villain effect fires when the villain is fought on a listed City space (index 0 = Sewers): the current player gains the Wound (D-24295).

The same effect is blocked when the villain is fought off the listed space (index 4 = Bridge, not Sewers): the gate fails closed and no Wound is gained. Paired with the on-space sibling that proves the effect fires (D-24295).

When a player's deck is empty, Melter's reveal reshuffles their discard into the deck first (the standard reveal-reshuffle rule, D-24285): the discarded card is now on the deck and revealed (D-24413).

A Melter choice parks over the reshuffled deck top — the reveal proceeded on the refilled deck, not a no-op on an empty one; had the reshuffle been skipped the deck would stay empty and no choice would park (D-24413).

gain-recruit-current (Hand Ninjas Fight reward) adds its magnitude to the defeating player's recruit for the turn — the first ruling asserting on the turn economy, via the new turn-economy-value expectation kind (D-24350).
When the current player gains a Wound, the handler bumps the UI-facing turnEconomy.woundsDrawn projection by one so the economy is not off-by-one (D-24023, the gain-wound primitive).

An each-player wound wounds every player but bumps woundsDrawn only ONCE, for the current player — the projection reports the current player's wounds only, so a two-player each-wound leaves woundsDrawn at 1 rather than 2 (D-24023).
draw-cards-current (Enchantress) draws its drawCount cards from the top of the current player's deck into their hand, in deck order (D-24290).
The drawn cards are removed from the top of the deck, leaving the undrawn remainder — proving the draw consumed the deck top rather than copying (D-24290).

A hero attack-grant effect adds its magnitude to the acting player's attack for the turn — the first hero-effect ruling, via the new fire-hero-effect action reaching the data-driven hero-effect executor (D-24022).
A hero recruit-grant effect adds its magnitude to the acting player's recruit — the fire-hero-effect action reaches the hero-effect executor for any MVP keyword, not just attack (D-24022).
A hero draw effect draws N cards and counts the realized draw toward turnEconomy.cardsDrawn — the per-turn effect-draw total the cardsDrawnThisTurnAtLeast gate reads (D-24476).
The hero draw moves the top N cards of the player's deck into their hand, in deck order (D-24022, the data-driven hero-effect dispatch / draw keyword).
A hero rescue effect moves a Bystander from the shared supply into the acting player's Victory pile (D-24017).
The rescue is bounded by the Bystander supply — magnitude 2 with one Bystander available rescues exactly one (D-24017).
A hero ko effect KOs the played card itself — the source card moves from in-play to the KO pile (D-24022, the ko keyword targets the played card).
The KO'd card is removed from in-play before it enters the KO pile — it is no longer in play (D-24022). Paired with the positive sibling that asserts it reached the KO pile.

D-2401 routes the scheme-twist handler through the executeRuleHooks → applyRuleEffects pipeline as an ImplementationMap entry, and buildGenericTwistEffects (schemeHandlers.ts) emits a modifyCounter schemeTwistCount delta:1 on every onSchemeTwistRevealed, so one reveal on a fresh state (schemeTwistCount absent = 0) leaves the counter at 1.

D-2403 (MVP Mastermind Strike Uses Counter + Message Only) has the mastermind-strike handler produce a modifyCounter masterStrikeCount delta:1 plus a queueMessage, so one onMastermindStrikeRevealed reveal on a fresh state (masterStrikeCount absent = 0) leaves the counter at 1.

Resolving one of a two-reveal Melter choice removes only that revealed top from the entry; the entry still holds the sibling reveal, so the choice is NOT front-popped and the queue stays length 1 (the entry pops only when its revealedTops list empties, D-24413).

A single resolve KOs only the chosen owner's revealed card (Player 0's Wound); the sibling reveal (Player 1's Hero) is untouched and still awaits its own resolve — one decision per revealed top (D-24413).
A resolve naming a card absent from the stated zone is a silent no-op: nothing is KO'd and the reward never fires, because the reward is atomic on an actual KO (D-24019).

The stale-target no-op leaves the pending entry in place so the player can resubmit a valid target — the queue is not front-popped on an invalid KO (D-24019). Paired with the sibling that proves nothing was KO'd.

With only one card to look at there is nothing to choose, so scry-ko-own-deck AUTO-KOs the sole deck-top card rather than parking a single-option choice that would freeze the board (D-24282 single-card carve-out).

With two or more cards the interactive upgrade parks one scry-ko choice for the player to pick which of the revealed top two to KO — restoring the agency the old auto-resolve removed (D-24282 / WP-470).

The interactive scry-ko KOs nothing at park time — the KO waits for the player's resolve; the old auto-resolve would have immediately KO'd the worse of the two cards (D-24282). Paired with the park-length sibling that proves the choice opened.
Resolving a parked scry-ko choice KOs the player's chosen card from the revealed top two (D-24282); the pick must be one of the revealed ext_ids (round-trip rule).
The un-chosen revealed card stays on top of the deck — only the picked card is removed, so the other of the two is kept (D-24282, 'the other stays on top').
Declining the optional KO leaves the board untouched — no card is KO'd and (since the reward is atomic on an actual KO) no reward fires (D-24019).

Unlike a stale-target no-op, an explicit decline front-pops the pending entry so the choice is resolved and the turn can end — the queue empties (D-24019). Paired with the sibling that proves nothing was KO'd.

With exactly one KO-able Hero the choice is forced, so a current-player ko-hero AUTO-KOs it rather than parking a single-option choice that would freeze the board (D-24007 decision C: one distinct option → auto-KO).

With two or more distinct KO-able Heroes there is a genuine choice of which to spare, so a current-player ko-hero parks one interactive choice for the player instead of auto-resolving (D-24007 / WP-242).
The interactive current-player ko-hero KOs nothing at park time — the KO waits for the player's pick (D-24007). Paired with the park-length sibling that proves the choice opened.
Resolving a parked KO-a-Hero choice KOs the player's chosen Hero from the named zone (D-24007); eligibility is recomputed against current G, so only a present target is accepted.
Only the chosen Hero is KO'd — the other eligible Hero is spared and stays in hand, which is the whole point of the interactive pick (D-24007).
Resolving a mandatory discard-to-play cost moves the chosen hand card out of hand to pay the cost — the remaining hand card is untouched (D-24184, WP-383).
The card discarded to pay the cost lands in the player's discard pile (through the WP-498 discard chokepoint), not the KO pile — a discard-to-play cost is a discard, not a KO (D-24184).
The Destroyer's Fight KOs ALL of the current player's Heroes matching the trait predicate ([team:shield]); the S.H.I.E.L.D. Hero is KO'd while the non-matching X-Men Hero is not (D-24290).
A Hero whose trait does not match the predicate is left in hand — the trait-filtered KO removes only the matching Heroes (D-24290). Paired with the sibling that proves the matching Hero was KO'd.

Baron Zemo rescues one Bystander per current-player Hero matching the trait ([team:avengers]) — two Avengers Heroes rescue two Bystanders to the Victory pile, and the non-matching X-Men Hero adds none (D-24290).
The per-matching-hero rescue is bounded by the Bystander supply: two matching Heroes but only one Bystander available rescues exactly one (D-24290).
HYDRA Kidnappers' beneficial 'may gain a S.H.I.E.L.D. Officer' auto-takes (pure upside, no choice): one Officer moves from the supply to the defeating player's discard (D-24350).
An empty Officer supply is a reachable no-op — nothing is gained and the player's discard stays empty (D-24350). Paired with the sibling that proves an Officer is gained when the supply has one.
Doctor Octopus's Fight sets the current player's next-hand fill target to an ABSOLUTE size (8, 'draw eight cards instead of six'), written to G.handSizeOverrides (D-24307).

Savage Land Mutates ADDS to the base hand size rather than replacing it: with no prior override the next-hand target becomes HAND_SIZE (6) + 1 = 7, so two defeats in a turn would stack (D-24352, contrast the absolute override-next-hand-size).

The rightmost selector scans the five HQ slots from index 4 down to 0 and captures the first non-null Hero, skipping empty slots: with heroes in slots 0/2/4 it captures slot 4 (Hulk) and attaches it to the villain's capture list (D-21401, WP-214 selector determinism).

The highest-cost selector reads G.cardStats[id].cost across the HQ and captures the costliest Hero — here Wolverine at cost 7 over Spider-Man (3) and Hulk (2) — proving the selector uses the cost stat, not slot position (D-21401, WP-214).

When two HQ Heroes tie on cost (both 5) the highest-cost selector breaks the tie by the RIGHTMOST slot index, capturing Wolverine (slot 2) over Spider-Man (slot 0) — the determinism contract that keeps the capture replayable regardless of scan order (D-21401, WP-214).

hero-deck-top-to-escape moves the TOP card of the shared hero-deck reservoir (G.heroDeck[0], Spider-Man) into the escaped pile — proving it takes index 0, not the card beneath it (D-18502, WP-185; the reservoir is the top-level G.heroDeck, not G.piles).

An empty hero-deck reservoir is a reachable silent no-op — nothing escapes and the escaped pile stays empty (D-18502, WP-185). Paired with the positive sibling that proves a card escapes when the reservoir is non-empty.

The un-counted capture-bystander fired on Escape attaches one Bystander from the supply to the escaping card's attached-bystander list (G.attachedBystanders), proving the capture ran off the Fight fire site (D-18603).

On Escape the auto-award is suppressed: the immediate award to the player's Victory pile happens ONLY on Fight (the post-award fire site), so an escape leaves the captured Bystander attached and the Victory pile empty — the villain got away with it (D-18603, contrast the onFight capture-bystander that awards to Victory). Paired with the sibling that proves the Bystander was attached.

Ultron's Fight (the KO-or-gift double-choice, collapsed to the co-op-dominant gift) gives the [hc:tech] HQ Hero to the CURRENT player's discard, never the victory pile (D-24327 gain-routes-to-discard): Iron Man (Tech) is gifted while Captain America (Strength) is left in the HQ — the trait predicate selects the recipient card (D-24335).

When no HQ Hero matches the trait predicate ([hc:tech]) the gift is a reachable no-op — nothing is removed from the HQ and the current player's discard stays empty (D-24335). Paired with the positive sibling that proves a matching Hero is gifted.

Paibok's Fight (D-24343 / D-24284 current-parks / others-auto split) resolves non-current players FIRST, each auto-gaining the highest-cost HQ Hero into their discard: the non-current player gains Captain America (cost 8) over Iron Man (3) and Hulk (5), proving the auto-gain uses the cost stat and routes to discard (D-24327).

After the non-current player auto-gains one HQ Hero (leaving two, since the empty hero-deck refills the vacated slot with null), the current (human) player faces a genuine which-Hero choice and parks exactly one give-hq-hero pending entry rather than auto-resolving (D-24343 / D-24284 current-parks). Paired with the sibling that proves the non-current auto-gain landed.

Whirlwind's Ambush (Rule B) swaps the entrance-side villain (index 0, Whirlwind) with the escape-side villain (index 4, Melter) — the maximum positional displacement. The middle villain (Ultron, index 2) and both henchmen (Hand Ninjas index 1, Doombot Legion index 3) are untouched — henchmen never swap and only the lowest/highest villain-occupied spaces move (D-24336, the engine's first City board-position manipulation).

Fewer than two Villains in the City is a reachable no-op: with a single Villain (Whirlwind) among four henchmen there is no second Villain to swap with, so the City row is unchanged (D-24336). Paired with the positive sibling that proves the swap fires with two or more Villains.

Maestro's Fight counts the current player's [hc:strength] Heroes (two) and KOs that many of their Heroes; when the count equals every KO-able Hero the KO is forced and auto-resolves, so both Heroes land in the KO pile (D-24353 — the trait supplies the COUNT, not the victims).

With no [hc:strength] Hero the trait count is zero, so Maestro KOs nothing — a reachable no-op, and the non-matching Covert Hero is never a victim (D-24353). Paired with the positive sibling that proves the counted KO fires.

Baron Zemo's Ambush captures a base 1 Bystander plus one per [team:avengers] Hero in the HQ: with two Avengers (Iron Man, Captain America) and one non-Avenger (Wolverine) the count is 1 + 2 = 3, all attached to Baron Zemo's captured-bystander list — attach-only, never awarded here (awarded at his defeat, D-18506 / D-24334).

The 1 + per-Avengers-HQ-Hero capture (count 3 here) is bounded by the Bystander supply: with only two Bystanders available exactly two attach and the loop stops (D-24334). Paired with the full-supply sibling that proves the base-plus-matching count.

Healing Factor's KO-a-Wound reward KOs exactly one Wound from the player's hand to the KO pile before granting the draw reward; the co-played Wolverine (a valuable Hero) is never a KO target — the target is filtered to the Wound token, which is why this family could not reuse the KO-any-card keyword (D-24183). The draw reward is a clean no-op here (empty deck + discard).

With no Wound in hand or discard the optional KO-a-Wound does nothing — nothing is KO'd (the valuable Hero is never KO'd) and no reward is granted (D-24183). Paired with the positive sibling that proves a Wound is KO'd when present.

Investigate looks at the top 2 deck cards (Hulk, Spider-Man) and draws the FIRST that matches the static criterion ([hc:covert]): Hulk (Strength) is skipped and Spider-Man (Covert) is drawn to hand — deterministic first-match in look order, no player choice (D-24373, the WP-564 static-criterion subset).

After drawing the matched Spider-Man, the non-selected looked-at card (Hulk) goes to the BOTTOM of the deck in look order, while the un-looked-at third card (Iron Man) is now on top: deck becomes [Iron Man, Hulk] (D-24373). Paired with the sibling that proves the matching card was drawn.

God of Thunder's 'You can use Recruit as Attack this turn.' sets the turn-scoped G.turnEconomy.recruitSpendableAsAttack conversion flag to true, so getSpendableAttack later folds unspent Recruit into the fight budget (D-24389 / WP-580).

recruit-as-attack is a permission flag, not a grant: it moves no resource total, so G.turnEconomy.attack stays 0 even though the conversion is 'applied' (WP-434) — the Recruit is spendable as Attack only via getSpendableAttack, never by inflating the attack counter (D-24389). Paired with the flag-set sibling.

Smash ('discard another card from your hand; if you do, +4 Attack') parks one PendingSmashDiscard when the hand holds another card to discard — the +N Attack is granted at resolve time only if the player discards, so the fire site parks the optional choice rather than granting immediately (D-24492).

With no other card in hand to discard there is nothing to Smash for, so no choice parks and no Attack is granted — a reachable no-op (D-24492). Paired with the sibling that proves the choice parks when a discardable card exists.

'Look at the top card of your deck. Discard it or put it back.' snapshots the revealed top and parks one PendingRevealTopDispose for the active player — the discard/keep disposition happens at resolve time, not at the fire site (D-24521, Tigra's Supernatural Senses).

An empty deck AND discard means nothing can be revealed on top (the reveal-reshuffle finds no cards), so no choice parks — a reachable no-op (D-24521). Paired with the sibling that proves the choice parks when the deck has a card.

Resolving a parked Smash choice by discarding a hand card grants the entry's +N Attack (4) — the discard is the paid cost and the Attack is the payoff, granted only AFTER the discard actually removes the card (D-24492, 'if you do, +N Attack').

Declining the Smash grants zero Attack — 'you MAY discard' makes declining a legal, no-cost choice, so no discard means no payoff (D-24492). Paired with the discard sibling that proves the +N Attack fires when the player does discard.

Resolving a parked reveal-top choice with disposition 'discard' moves the revealed deck-top card from its owner's deck to that owner's discard pile (D-24521); the disposition applies only while the card is still the live deck top.

Resolving with disposition 'top' ('put it back') is a no-op on the deck — the reveal never removed the card, so it stays face-up on top and the deck is unchanged (D-24521). Paired with the discard sibling that proves the card moves when discarded.

Avengers Assemble!'s 'for each color of Hero you have' counts the distinct Hero colors among the Heroes you HAVE = hand + play area, order-independent (D-24529, rulebook "'Your Heroes/Allies' & 'Heroes/Allies You Have'"). Avengers Assemble! (Instinct) in play plus an unplayed Arc Reactor (Tech) still in hand = 2 colors → +2 Recruit, even though only the Instinct card was played. The pre-fix play-area-only reading gave +1.

Grey S.H.I.E.L.D. cards (Agent / Officer / Trooper) have NO Hero Class, so they add no color to 'for each color of Hero you have' (D-24529, rulebook Grey Heroes + Spectrum 'don't have classes, so they don't help'). A hand of two grey Heroes contributes nothing; only the Instinct Avengers Assemble! counts → +1 Recruit. The flip side of D-24345's 'heroClass != null means has a color, never is a Hero'.

A dual-class Hero in hand contributes BOTH its printed colors to 'color of Hero you have' (D-24529 hand ∪ play scope × D-24523 dual-class): Avengers Assemble! (Instinct) in play plus Heir to Legends (Strength + Ranged) unplayed in hand = 3 distinct colors → +3 Recruit.

Resolving a parked give-HQ-Hero choice moves the CHOSEN HQ Hero (Iron Man) into the chooser's DISCARD pile, never the victory pile (D-24327 gain-routes-to-discard); the untaken Captain America stays in the HQ (D-24343 / WP-532).

Paibok's give-HQ-Hero is MANDATORY (not an optional 'may recruit' tactic), so a decline is a no-op — nothing is gained and the discard stays empty; the player must still pick (D-24343; the decline arm is honored only for optional entries per D-24509). Paired with the gain sibling that proves a chosen Hero lands in discard.
Black Knight's 'return a 0-cost card from your discard to your hand' (Defend the Weak) moves the chosen 0-cost card (the cost-0 S.H.I.E.L.D. Agent) from discard into hand (D-24139).

A non-0-cost discard card (Wolverine, cost 3) is not a legal target for the 0-cost-return ability, so the resolve is a no-op — nothing enters the hand (D-24139, the 0-cost eligibility filter). Paired with the sibling that proves a 0-cost card returns.

Accepting the Do-Over discards the ENTIRE current hand and then draws a FIXED 4 cards (not one-per-discard): the two-card hand is discarded and the top four deck cards become the new hand (D-24498, Deadpool's 'Hey, Can I Get a Do-Over?').

Declining the Do-Over ('you may discard the rest of your hand') is a no-op — nothing is discarded and nothing is drawn, so the hand is unchanged (D-24498). Paired with the accept sibling that proves the discard-and-redraw fires.

Absorb Ambient Power's mandatory put-a-card-on-the-deck-bottom grants its icon reward when the moved card HAS the matching icon: the moved card is seeded with a recruit icon (recruit 1), so the player gains +3 recruit (D-24133). Paired with the no-icon sibling — same card, no icon, no reward — which isolates that the reward keys on the icon, not the card.

The SAME moved card seeded WITHOUT a recruit or attack icon (recruit 0, attack 0) grants no reward — the +N is conditional on the moved card's printed icon, so it stays at 0 recruit (D-24133). Paired with the recruit-icon sibling that proves the reward fires when the icon is present.

Ebony Blade's 'claim the printed Attack of a Villain in your Victory pile' grants attack equal to the chosen villain's printed attack, stored as fightCost on villain cards (their .attack is always 0): the Lizard's fightCost 5 → +5 attack (D-24067 / WP-285).

Only cards typed 'villain' in G.villainDeckCardTypes are eligible — a henchman (Doombot Legion) in the Victory pile is not a valid Ebony Blade target, so the pick is a no-op and no attack is granted despite its fightCost (D-24067). Paired with the villain sibling that proves the attack claim fires.

Loki's Maniacal Tyrant ('KO up to four cards from your discard pile') KOs exactly the chosen distinct discard cards to the general KO pile: the two selected (Wolverine, Spider-Man) land in G.ko while the unselected Hulk stays in discard (D-24510 / WP-693).

A selection larger than the printed cap (two cards chosen against maxCount 1) is an invalid payload — the whole resolve is a no-op and nothing is KO'd, leaving the queue intact so the player resubmits within the cap (D-24510). Paired with the in-cap sibling that proves the KO fires.

Gambit's Stack the Deck puts the chosen hand card on TOP of the deck (deck[0], drawn first next): Wolverine is prepended ahead of the existing Hulk, so the deck becomes [Wolverine, Hulk] (D-24519 / WP-700).

The card placed on the deck top leaves the hand — the mandatory placement moves it hand→deck, so only the unchosen Spider-Man remains in hand (D-24519). Paired with the deck-top sibling that proves the card lands on top of the deck.

The Undercover choice sends the chosen eligible [team:shield] Hero from hand to the Victory Pile (worth 1 VP): the picked Nick Fury copy lands in victory while the other stays in hand (D-24494 / WP-678).

A target not in the parked eligible snapshot cannot be sent Undercover — resolving with an ineligible copy is a no-op, so the Victory Pile stays empty (the round-trip eligibility gate, D-24494). Paired with the sibling that proves an eligible Hero is sent.
Magneto's Master Strike ('discard down to four cards') makes a 6-card hand discard exactly two to reach the limit of 4: the two chosen cards move hand→discard through the WP-498 chokepoint (D-24284).

The discard must land EXACTLY on the limit — discarding one card from a 6-card hand would leave 5, not 4, so the wrong-count selection is a whole-move no-op and nothing is discarded (D-24284). Paired with the exactly-to-limit sibling that proves the discard fires.

Dr. Doom's Master Strike puts exactly count (2) hand cards on TOP of the deck in selection order (cardIds[0] ends at deck[0], drawn first): [Wolverine, Spider-Man] prepend ahead of the existing Iron Man → deck [Wolverine, Spider-Man, Iron Man] (D-24347).

The selection must be EXACTLY count cards — one card against count 2 is an invalid payload, so the whole resolve is a no-op and the deck is unchanged (D-24347). Paired with the exact-count sibling that proves the placement fires.

The Amazing Spider-Man's 'put the rest back in any order' rewrites the top-N of the deck to the player's chosen order: the two-card remainder [Wolverine, Spider-Man] is reordered to [Spider-Man, Wolverine] while the un-revealed Hulk below is untouched (D-24286, a pure permutation — no card added or dropped).

The submitted order must be a PERMUTATION of the parked remainder — including Hulk (which is below the remainder, not part of it) is not a permutation of [Wolverine, Spider-Man], so the whole resolve is a no-op and the deck is unchanged (D-24286, no card added or dropped). Paired with the valid-permutation sibling that proves the reorder fires.

One-Hit Wonder's 'Choose one: Draw a card, or you get Empowered' — picking 'draw' draws the top deck card into hand (Spider-Man), reusing the shared draw executor (D-24069). Paired with the empowered sibling that proves the other half of the choose-one.

Picking 'empowered' grants +Attack equal to the count of the empowered class in the HQ (Empowered by [hc:tech] = +1 per Tech Hero in the HQ): two Tech Heroes (Iron Man, Nick Fury) among a Strength Hulk → +2 attack (D-24069, count-cards-by-class-in-zone over the HQ). Paired with the draw sibling.

Wonder Man's 8th Wonder of the World / Sunspot's Empyreal Force 'Choose any number of cards from the HQ; put them on the bottom of the Hero Deck' - each chosen HQ card is pushed to the Hero Deck bottom and its vacated slot refills from the deck top (the recruitHero refill path), never leaving a permanent gap. Selecting Spider-Man (slot 1) then Wolverine (slot 3) refills those slots with Storm then Rogue, in submitted order (D-24132).

The trailing 'Then you get Empowered by [hc:tech]' grant fires AFTER the HQ is reshaped, so it counts the reshaped HQ, not the original (D-24132, printed order). Putting the Tech Iron Man (slot 0) on the deck bottom refills slot 0 with the Strength Hulk from the deck top, dropping the HQ Tech count from two (Iron Man + Nick Fury) to one (Nick Fury) - so Empowered by Tech grants +1 attack, not +2. Had the count run before the move it would read +2; this ruling pins the after-the-reshape ordering.
